subject: Incorporate other types of random effects in TMB

messages.author: e5c7e56038437512
messages.subject: Incorporate other types of random effects in TMB
parts:
Hi!

I hope that all of you are ok.
I would like incorporate other type of random effect (spatial random effect) in TMB, specifically a Thin Plate Spline. The Thin Plate Spline is built through of basis functions and also can be an option to modeling spatial observations without specify a covariance function.
There are an example in c++ and matlab about this. For the above I have a question.
¿Is possible incorporate that code (c++) into of TMB directly or is neccesary other previous step? 

Best regards

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Incorporate other types of random effects in TMB
parts:
Hi, I think this should be possible if you set up the spline basis using mgcv and import it into TMB.
You should be able to build on the 1 dimensional spline example "pSplines" from:
https://github.com/skaug/tmb-case-studies

However, I should say that I have never tried this with thin plate splines.

Thanks Hans!

Yes, I also think that is possible incorporate directly from 'mgcv' library using 's' for a thin plate spline in 2D. That is an option.

I'm working in my PhD thesis and my idea is build directly the Thin Plate Spline as a random effect in TMB (with some differences in comparison by the proposal by Wood, 2003 that uses the library 'mgcv')
I have seen an example of a Thin Plate Spline in c++ and I think that we could do it..  in theory.
I should see the example that you say for a Psplines in 1D.

Thanks!
